question.prompt: A rhombus has diagonals of lengths \(6\) and \(8\). What are its side length and area? (Answer in this order, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: The diagonals are perpendicular and bisect each other, so the side length is \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\). The area is \(6\times8\div2=24\).
solutions.title: Use the perpendicular half-diagonals
